justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: Pelvic floor PT produces meaningful incontinence reduction; PRPC certification vs non-certified comparison not studied.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: Multi-course PRPC pathway requires significant clinical experience plus exam; major investment.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Applicable to pelvic health specialty practice; growing population but requires specialized equipment and setting.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: Pelvic floor PT billed under standard PT codes; growing commercial coverage; PRPC supports women's health and pelvic health program billing.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Rapidly growing employer demand as pelvic health PT becomes mainstream; increasingly listed in women's health postings.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: High when outcomes achieved; significant stigma around seeking care is barrier.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: Pelvic health is arguably the strongest cash-pay niche in PT — patients routinely pay $150-$250/session out of pocket.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: Scarcity of trained clinicians and high patient motivation enables premium pricing nationwide.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: PRPC is recognized but less dominant than Herman & Wallace's PF series; still clearly differentiating in most markets.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Pelvic-only clinics scale well by hiring additional PRPC/H&W-trained clinicians with consistent protocols.
justifications.business.marketDemand: Strong and growing consumer demand driven by postpartum, menopause, and men's pelvic awareness.
justifications.business.efficiency: Coursework is multi-course and time-intensive but ROI per dollar of training is exceptional.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: Recognized as legitimate specialty competency but Women's Health CS (WCS) carries more academic weight.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: Pelvic health literature is expanding rapidly with active researchers, though PRPC holders aren't dominant in journals.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Pelvic health is increasingly required content in DPT curricula; trained faculty are in short supply.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Strong evidence for PFMT in incontinence and pelvic pain; emerging for other indications.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Programs do recruit pelvic-trained faculty, though they prefer WCS when available.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Faster and cheaper than achieving WCS while still teaching most curricular content.
